changes.summary: group setup and hook adapters under system
changes.body:
Automation uses `beeswax system prepare`, `system hooks`, `system harness-alert`,
`system beads session-start`, `system git merge` and `system git validate-staged`.
The former paths are removed. Ordinary tracker operations and `beeswax git pack`
remain public.

Required: update consuming projects after installing the matching Beeswax release:

- Prepare the permanent tracker's configured hook files with the current v2
  validation section before binding it. Binding requires that exact section and
  never rewrites tracked tracker hooks.
- Run `beeswax update --yes` to upgrade recognized ordinary v1 validation sections,
  regenerate owned harness adapters, refresh the project lock and rebind the Git
  merge driver to `system git merge`. Preserve surrounding hook code. Unrecognized
  or edited state needs the explicit resolution described by `beeswax migrate hooks`
  or `beeswax migrate setup`; update alone does not resolve it.
- Update application-owned prepare scripts to `beeswax system prepare`, session
  hooks to `beeswax system beads session-start`, snapshot exemptions to
  `beeswax system hooks is-tracker-snapshot`, and direct staged-validation calls to
  `beeswax system git validate-staged`. These application-owned calls are not
  regenerated by Beeswax.
- Commit the reviewed project contract and generated files, then run `beeswax sync`
  in each adopting checkout to refresh its local binding. Existing harness sessions
  must load and trust the changed adapters.
breaking: group setup and hook adapters under system

changes.summary: deliver tracker alerts and manual recovery guidance
changes.body:
Failed native reconciliation or Git publication now records a user-local alert
keyed by the selected database path. Use `beeswax beads alert status` or bounded
`beeswax beads alert wait` to observe it without opening SQLite, and
`beeswax beads recover` for the non-mutating manual recovery handoff. An active
incident holds ordinary publication; clearance requires successful, explicitly
authorized recovery publication for that exact incident.

Managed Claude Code, Codex and Pi adapters supply advisory hold and clearance
guidance at supported callbacks. They neither exclude native writers nor stop
workers, and idle sessions receive no immediate push. Independent non-Beads
work may continue while tracker work pauses; notices grant no recovery authority.

Required to receive harness notices after upgrading: run `beeswax update --yes`
in each adopting project to refresh its selected managed adapters. To select
additional harnesses, see `beeswax update --help`. Start new sessions in checkouts
containing those adapters with the upgraded Beeswax on PATH. In Codex, trust the
project and review and trust changed hooks through `/hooks`; in Pi, grant project
trust for extension loading. Verify hold and clearance delivery in each harness
before relying on it. Validation covers callback contracts and Pi SDK context
composition; live Claude Code and Codex model delivery remains untested.

changes.summary: relocate the Hive workflow skill source
changes.body:
The optional hive workflow skill now lives at lib/beeswax/skills/hive.
Beeswax setup and the documented manual installer use
https://github.com/codethread/hive/tree/main/lib/beeswax/skills/hive.
The skill content is unchanged. Hive also adopts it locally through the
upstream installer, retaining its project copy and generated lock entry.

Required: update saved installer commands that use the former public source
URL to the new URL. If using Beeswax setup to install the skill, upgrade to
a Beeswax release with the new source URL first.

Optional: install the skill for a consuming repository that wants these
customizable work conventions. Follow beeswax setup --help or the Beeswax
README's skill-only installer example and review the installed files.
Existing installed copies need no migration; Beeswax sync and update leave
them unchanged.

BREAKING CHANGE: the public source moves from skills/hive to
lib/beeswax/skills/hive. Saved installer URLs and older Beeswax releases
still target the removed source path.

changes.summary: include Beads and BV in portable task guidance
changes.body:
`beeswax prime` now includes `br` and `bv` by default. Shared guidance covers tracker identity, system-record filtering, task authority, claims, human reservations, verification and publication checkpoints. Tool-row filters retain this safety baseline. Prime works offline without a source checkout, tracker or installed skill. Release-history pointers remain limited to Hive-owned CLIs.

Optional: read `beeswax prime --help` for defaults and filters. Consolidate repeated safety guidance around one primer loading route while retaining repository-specific policy.

changes.summary: install a customizable Hive workflow during setup
changes.body:
Setup offers `--install-workflow-skill` and a default-off wizard choice. It installs only the public `hive` skill for selected Claude Code, Codex or Pi harnesses through `skills@1.7.2`. Installation requires Node >=22.20.0, npm/npx and network access; prime remains offline.

Existing skill destinations stop setup before writes. Installation runs last; failures retain completed setup phases and installer diagnostics for review of partial effects. The opt-in is not saved. Prime, hooks, sync and update never install or refresh the skill.

Optional: read `beeswax setup --help` before adding the flag to an intended setup invocation; `--yes` alone does not opt in. Omit the flag to preserve an existing workflow. Customize and commit installed files, selected links and installer metadata, then verify discovery and trust in each execution checkout. Review upstream replacements manually: the public main-branch skill evolves independently of the executable. Codex and Pi share its canonical project directory.

changes.summary: omit unavailable tools from update history pointers
changes.body:
`beeswax update` returns history commands only for known Hive tool names
found on `PATH`, including Waggle when present. It checks executable names,
not tool versions or supported subcommands.

After upgrading Hive's executables, refresh the project contract and follow
the returned history commands:

```sh
beeswax update --yes
```

The previous project version remains the exclusive `--since` baseline;
same-version updates point to current history without `--since`. This fix
requires no manual migration. Updating the contract does not install binaries
or apply or acknowledge adoption actions.

changes.summary: link project updates to offline tool histories
changes.body:
Use `beeswax changelog` to read bundled release changes and adoption
instructions. After upgrading, run `beeswax update --yes` in each adopting
project to refresh its saved contract and onboarding. The update reports
the previous and installed versions, with `<tool> changelog --since VERSION`
commands using the previous project version. Same-version updates point
to the current history without `--since`. Prime also directs agents to
changelogs after upgrades.

Updating the project lock does not apply or acknowledge adoption actions.

adoption.text: Review the tool histories linked by beeswax update for changes and adoption actions relevant to the project.

changes.summary: Setup reports configured artifacts, pending readiness checks and completed phases after partial failures.
